# Warp v0.1.0

First public release of Warp, a Go/Bubble Tea layout framework for terminal UIs.

## Highlights

- Split and flex layouts with deterministic geometry, dragging, collapse controls, tabs, floating panes, modals, popovers, dropdowns, inputs, scrolling, and selectable text.
- Semantic UI tree for testing and automation, including framework-owned tab/float/input/dropdown/collapse chrome.
- Optional HTTP inspector with immutable UI-thread snapshots, secure CORS defaults, bearer-token support, bounded shutdown, and cached JSON responses.
- Resource lifecycle support through optional `Unmounter`, with ownership domains and exactly-once cleanup when the final owned reference is removed.
- Grapheme-aware Unicode input, rendering, selection, and terminal-safe framework labels.

## Reliability and security

- Semantic trees are bounded to 128 levels and 100,000 nodes.
- Framework labels normalize invalid UTF-8 and neutralize ANSI/OSC and raw layout-control injection.
- Inspector snapshots are invalidated on root replacement and refreshed after rendering.
- Floating panels preserve Bubble Tea mouse modifiers and compatibility fields.
- Popover hover hit testing is constrained to the visible menu content.
- `govulncheck` reports no reachable vulnerabilities.

## Performance

- Inspector work is completely avoided when disabled.
- `SemanticStableMsg` lets high-frequency messages reuse semantic snapshots until the next render.
- On the M1 Pro audit benchmark with 10,000 semantic elements, stable-message updates run in roughly 0.2–0.34 µs with zero allocations, versus roughly 0.20–0.23 ms and ~1.04 MB/op for a full semantic rebuild.
- Renderer allocation pressure has been reduced through per-frame blank/border reuse, exact row materialization, flex preallocation, and reduced nested split normalization.

## Compatibility and verification

- Module language baseline: Go 1.22.
- CI verifies Go 1.22, 1.26, and 1.27 on Linux, plus Go 1.27 on macOS and Windows.
- Release gating includes formatting, vet, tests, race detector, shuffled/repeated tests, fuzz smoke, golangci-lint, govulncheck, and a 90% core coverage floor.

Install:

```bash
go get github.com/starframe-dev/warp@v0.1.0
```

## Notes

Warp intentionally remains on the current Charm dependency stack for this release. Newer Bubble Tea/Lip Gloss combinations were benchmarked during release hardening and showed measurable allocation/runtime regressions while also raising the minimum Go requirement. Dependency upgrades will be revisited with explicit benchmarks.
